title: Surge Capacity Sprint Playbook: Retail & Marketing Traffic Spikes
author: Priya Nambiar
body:
Overview

This playbook defines the on-call procedures, runbooks, communication templates, and post-incident analysis steps for rapid capacity surges driven by retail or marketing campaigns (flash sales, promotional emails, sponsored ad pushes). It focuses on containment, fast-path capacity ramp, graceful degradation for non-critical features, and customer communication. Use this when traffic grows 2x+ above normal sustained TPS for >5 minutes or when latency SLOs cross the warning threshold for core APIs.

Scope and assumptions

- Scope: Redwood public API endpoints (generation, embeddings, streaming), regional load balancers, autoscaler control plane, KV cache layer, and customer-facing status page.
- Assumptions: Autoscaling is enabled for affected fleets; dedicated capacity customers may be exempt; telemetry (awssignals / prometheus) is operational.
- Exclusions: Internal CI jobs, scheduled maintenance windows, or slow-degrading experiments are handled by separate maintenance runbooks.

Severity classification (specialized for surge events)

1) Surge-S1 — transient spike: short-lived spike ( < 10 minutes ), no SLO breach, warnings in latency percentiles.
2) Surge-S2 — sustained surge: >= 2x baseline for >= 10 minutes, 95th percentile latency > SLO but error rate < 0.5%.
3) Surge-S3 — capacity saturation: error rates > 0.5% and client-visible failures or denied capacity.

Quick triage checklist (first 10 minutes)

1. Acknowledge alert and create an incident channel (Slack #inc-surge-<region>-<time>) and Zoom bridge.
2. Capture starter evidence (one-line): "What, where, when, impact" and pin to channel.
3. Identify the signal: traffic volume, RPC queue depth, GPU utilization, autoscaler events, upstream DDoS protection logs.
4. If traffic originates from a single customer or IP bloc, flag for tenant-aware mitigation (see Tenant Containment).
5. Start customer-facing status notice (template below) in draft.

Roles and responsibilities

- Incident Lead (first on-call): overall coordination, declaring severity, and customer notices.
- Capacity Engineer: tune autoscaler, provision burst pools, and perform pool-level restarts if needed.
- Routing/Edge Engineer: validate LB health, remove noisy backends, apply traffic shaping.
- Product Owner (on-call for product): approve graceful-degradation choices and feature toggles.
- Customer Success/Support Liaison: prepare customer-specific comms for affected accounts.

Containment steps (Surge-S2 / Surge-S3)

1) Fast-fail non-essential routes
   - For routes serving analytics, batch embeddings, or background tasks, toggle feature_gate=defer_background (example CLI):
     rdc toggle-feature --route "/v1/embeddings/batch" --flag defer_background --until 1h
   - Immediately disable optional streaming websockets for low-tier traffic.

2) Tenant containment
   - If a single tenant causes the spike: apply tenant throttles (soft limit 20 rps) and move to a dedicated rate-limited pool.
   - Commands: 
     - List top tenants by qps: curl -s https://telemetry.internal/api/top-tenants | jq '.'
     - Apply throttle: rdc tenant-rate --tenant <id> --limit 20

3) Scale-up and pre-warm
   - Trigger manual burst capacity for the affected region (owner: Capacity Engineer).
   - AWS example: runbook includes IaC shortcut: terraform apply -var=\"burst=true\" -target=module.pools.burst
   - Pre-warm caches: run cache-warm job for the top N prefixes for expected inputs.

4) Backpressure and client hints
   - Emit 429 with Retry-After for best-effort degradations. Prefer 202/accepted for queued batch work.

Recovery and restoration steps

1. Confirm saturation has reduced for >2 consecutive 5-minute windows (traffic and GPU util).
2. Remove temporary throttles and feature gates in reverse order (document each change in channel).
3. Drain and decommission temporary burst nodes once warm utilization < 50% for 15 minutes.
4. Run sanity checks: sample a set of golden prompts across model families and validate p99 latency and correctness.

Operational playbook snippets and commands

- List affected autoscaler events: rdc autoscaler events --region us-west-2 --since 30m
- Promote burst pool: rdc pool promote --name burst-usw2 --until 02:00
- Re-route traffic away from unhealthy LB: rdc lb adjust --lb api-west --remove backend-id=be-1234

Customer and public status templates

Internal short status (first 15 minutes)

"Status: We are investigating a traffic surge impacting inference latency for US-West customers. Core APIs are slower than normal; some batch requests are queued. Incident lead: @<name>. Next update: in 15 minutes."

Public status page (short)

Title: "Degraded performance for inference in US-West due to unexpected traffic surge"
Impact: "Some requests may experience elevated latency or temporary queueing. A subset of background jobs may be delayed."
Mitigation: "We have enabled temporary burst capacity and are throttling non-essential routes to restore responsiveness."
Updates: "We will post updates every 15 minutes."

Customer-specific email template (for high-touch accounts)

Subject: "[Action Required] Temporary throughput controls during US-West traffic surge"
Body: "Hello <CustomerName>, we detected a significant traffic surge impacting your region and have applied temporary throughput controls to protect availability. Recommended actions: reduce parallel client threads and defer large batch submissions for 30–60 minutes. Our team is actively scaling and will follow up when controls are removed. — Redwood Inference Support"

Game day scenarios and exercises (recommended cadence: quarterly)

Scenario A — "BlackFriday Sim": synthetic traffic ramp 10x baseline with multi-tenant noisy neighbor injection. Objectives: verify tenant containment automation, autoscaler burst IRS, and status cadence.
Scenario B — "Promo Blast": A single high-traffic tenant ramps to 5x; objective: confirm tenant throttle workflow and customer comm loop.
Scenario C — "Cache Eviction Storm": KV cache misses lead to GPU pressure; objective: validate cache-warm and pre-warm scripts and golden prompt verification.

Exercise checklist (for each game day)

- Pre-game: validate telemetry pipelines, create synthetic keys, and reserve burst quota.
- During: time-boxed changes, one change per 5 minutes, record timestamps.
- Post-game: run the postmortem template below and publish learnings.

Post-incident analysis and postmortem template

Required artifacts to attach:
- Incident timeline (UTC) with exact actions and authors.
- Telemetry graphs: TPS, p50/p95/p99, error-rate, GPU util, queue depth, autoscaler events.
- List of toggles/throttles and exact CLI commands used.
- Customer impact list (accounts with failed requests or elevated latencies).
- Root cause hypothesis and severity rationale.

Postmortem sections (copy into a standard page)

1. Summary — 1–2 sentence description and business impact.
2. Timeline — minute-by-minute sequence.
3. Impact — systems, customers, SLO breaches.
4. Root cause analysis — technical explanation and evidence.
5. Actions planned — owner, due date, verification criteria.
6. Retro notes — what worked, what didn't, and recommended game-day changes.

Example postmortem action items

- Automate tenant throttling into the autoscaler pipeline (owner: eng-serving-runtime; due: 2026-04-15).
- Instrument early-warning signal: moving-average QPS over 3 minutes (owner: eng-sre; due: 2026-03-31).
- Add a customer-visible field to status notices for high-touch accounts (owner: customer-success; due: 2026-04-07).

Runbook governance and maintenance

- This playbook must be reviewed after every Surge-S2 or Surge-S3 incident and during quarterly game days.
- Runbook owner: Capacity Engineering Guild. Review cadence: quarterly.

Appendix: quick decision ladder (one-liners)

- If p99 latency > 2x SLO and error rate < 0.5%: flip non-essential feature gates and trigger burst pool.
- If error rate > 0.5%: apply tenant containment and consider regional traffic re-route.
- If burst pool fails to provision in 10 minutes: escalate to infra on-call and prepare customer credit assessment.

Links and references

- Tenant containment procedure: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/tenant-containment-manual-2024

Contact matrix (escalation)

- 0–10 minutes: Incident Lead (oncall-primary)
- 10–30 minutes: Add Capacity Engineer and Routing Engineer
- 30+ minutes: Pager to Eng Director and Customer Success Director
